key_insight: Rice husk ash can be converted into silica powders that are amorphous after 800 °C treatment and crystallize into quartz/cristobalite after 1200 °C annealing, enabling tailored feedstock for thermal spray use.
engineering_relevance: This offers a low-cost, biomass-derived route to silica powder materials with tunable structure for coating and thermal spray applications.
method: Chemically treated rice husk ash to extract silica precursor.
Heat-treated at 800 °C for 3 h to obtain amorphous SiO2 powder.
Annealed at 1200 °C to induce crystalline quartz and cristobalite phases.
evidence_signal: XRD, FTIR, and laser diffraction confirmed phase evolution, Si–O–Si bonding, and a median particle size of about 88.9 μm.
watch_item: High-temperature crystallization can change powder flowability and spray behavior, so phase control and particle size distribution should be checked before coating trials.
paper_title: Synthesis of Amorphous and Crystalline Silicon Dioxide Powder Composites from Rice Husk Ash for Thermal Spray Deposit
